correctness.rationale: Take the eight length-four outputs T with second and fourth bits equal. Every six-bit word has a burst deletion in T by the three-pair pigeonhole principle, giving |C|≤8 for disjoint shadows. Equality forces one representative from each of eight explicit buckets. Independent complete enumeration over all 64 six-bit inputs gives bucket sizes 5,4,5,4,4,5,4,5 and exact search-tree node counts 1,5,13,28,17,8,11,2,2, with precisely the two displayed eight-word codes. Both yield 16 pairwise disjoint received outputs and are linear three-dimensional F2 subspaces. This is a genuine complete finite proof, not a partial search; boundaries are fixed exactly two adjacent deleted symbols, not arbitrary or one-bit deletion.
residual_risks: No statement beyond binary word length six or burst exactly two.
